Demonology Scenario Stepper

16 states of one Cooldown Manager row, walked left to right. Each icon carries a verdict — what Combat Assist Plus concluded about that button — and the walk names why every available button is skipped until the press.

The reading model: scan left to right and press the first button that is not ruled out. The press is not something cap draws — press and open render identically. Blizzard's swipe says skip this; a red badge says skip this, and why. The vocabulary is negative by default: a satisfied dependency draws nothing at all. Two cues are positive and scoped — capped (impending loss) and priority (press this one) — and no single entry ever wears more than one of them.

Rendered from specs/demonology/scenarios.json + scenarios.md and specs/render-tokens.json. Real Blizzard icon art at the client's 56 px, real vendored sprite frames at their real frame counts, and cap's treatments composited the way the client composites them — SetVertexColor as a multiply, never a hue rotation. This is a preview of what the addon would draw, not a diagram of it.

The row, in a state

The primitives — every treatment the shelf declares, as a live swatch — are their own page. The style vocabulary is byte-identical on every spec page, so drawing it five times said five times that it was five different things.

Per-ability states

The authored source of truth, drawn. Every row of every table below comes from catalog.json — the same file that generates Catalogs/<Spec>.lua — so the addon, this page and the definition cannot disagree by construction. A scenario walk shows one line through these states; this shows all of them, including the ones no walk reaches.

Under each state, its provenance: the rung of the upstream priority list it comes from — resolved and quoted where it resolves — or one sentence saying why no rung covers it. Every state carries exactly one of the two. Beside it, the primitives that put it on screen, by registry id. ⚠ The rung citation is display-only: nothing here asserts that the quoted line still says what it said when it was cited. That is wowkb.simc --kb --check’s job.

Verdicts

The closed vocabulary. A verdict says what cap concluded; the shelf says what that looks like.

Everything on this page is the declared style. The lab — Part 7, experiments drawn so they can be looked at but not adopted — is its own page, because it belongs to render-shelf.md rather than to any spec: its cells resolve against the shelf’s reference roster, so drawing it under a spec’s heading invited the reading that it said something about that spec.
